description: We are STELLARYS, a team of interior architecture and graphic design students from Peru. We design interactive learning spaces that help schoolchildren explore the Moon and Mars through the missions and equipment NASA left behind, turning real data into stories they can walk through.
summary: What if a rover left on Mars could tell you its story? STELLARYS is an interactive web museum for children ages 8 to 12 that brings to life NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars. We created it for the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge, using NASA mission records and photographs to turn real hardware into first-person storytellers. Children can walk through a 3D museum, explore a 360° tour, or read the exhibits directly in English or Spanish. Each story connects a piece of equipment to the science it made possible.
details:
Our team of interior design and graphic design students from Peru created three exhibits about different ways to do science on another world. Sojourner tells how it drove up to Martian rocks and used an instrument to find out what they were made of. The Apollo 11 laser reflector explains how scientists measure the distance to the Moon by timing a pulse of light on its round trip. The Apollo 15 lunar rover shows how astronauts traveled farther from their landing site and collected samples from different locations.

In the 3D museum, visitors walk up to displays to open the stories. The 360° tour lets them move through five connected spaces by selecting doors. A separate story gallery gives readers direct access to all three exhibits, with mission photographs and links to NASA sources.

Tech Stack

- Astro, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS for the website.

- Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Blender for the walkable 3D museum.

- Photo Sphere Viewer for the interactive 360° tour.

Innovation Highlights

- The equipment tells its own story. Each exhibit starts with what the object did and connects that action to what scientists learned.

- Interior design guides discovery. The layout, displays, and doorways let children choose where to go and which stories to open.

- Visitors set their own pace. Stories are available in English and Spanish, and Calm Mode reduces decorative motion.
